points: Q3 2026 is the live quarter, and the Oct 29 print will show whether Coinbase can stop the deterioration that reports suggest produced a $359M net loss on $1.2B revenue in Q2.

The stock's own estimate direction is sharply negative — a 90-day revenue revision of -296.88% and 0 up/15 down analyst moves in the last 30 days — so the report will reveal whether estimates have finally priced in the weakness or still need to fall.
FY1 EPS is -1.99 versus FY2 EPS of +2.83, implying a big 2027 turnaround; Q3 guidance and management commentary will show whether that rebound has any operational support or is just analyst hope.
Reports suggest Q2 crypto trading volume fell 25% despite a record 10.3% market share; Q3 will reveal whether share gains are merely masking a shrinking overall market.
Reports also highlight stablecoin and services revenue as a source of diversification; Q3 will show whether non-trading revenue is still accelerating or starting to fade as trading revenue weakens.
Peer prints from NDAQ (Oct 22), PYPL (Oct 27), GDDY (Oct 28) and SEZL (Nov 6) will provide read-throughs on transaction volumes, take rates and fintech demand around COIN's report.
With a P/S ratio of 19.1, the valuation has little cushion for a revenue miss or further estimate cuts, so a soft Q3 would reinforce the short.
watch: 30-day analyst revisions stay 0 up/15 down or worsen — supports the short.
Q3 revenue follows the 90-day estimate collapse (-296.88% revision) and comes in weak — supports the short.
FY2 EPS turnaround to +2.83 looks less credible after Q3 guidance — supports the short.
P/S of 19.1x compresses on weaker revenue/estimates — supports the short.
